newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch DOCdata seeks Amsterdam, NASDAQ listings.
newsitem.headline: Dutch DOCdata seeks Amsterdam, NASDAQ listings.

text.p: Compact disc maker DOCdata BV said on Wednesday it would apply for a listing on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange and the U.S.-based electronic NASDAQ exchange.
The company plans to float five million shares, three million of which will be newly issued. After this issue, the total number of outstanding shares will be eight million.
"The expected introduction price of the shares will be between 24.38 and 28.13 guilders," DOCdata said in a statement. It added it would use the proceeds to pay debts and to finance future takeovers.
The shares will be offered in the Netherlands, the U.S. and other countries. Credit Suisse First Boston will act as lead manager.
DOCdata produces compact discs and laser systems and offers related services. The firm has outlets in the Netherlands, France, Germany and the U.S.

DOCdata was sold by industrial investment group Begemann in a management buy-out in 1995. After this transaction, DOCdata's management owned 31.5 percent of the shares and the other shares were owned by Citicorp, ABN AMRO and Dutch venture capital firm Gilde.
DOCdata has about 400 employees and posted 1995 turnover of 100 million guilders.
